consistent-selector-style/invalid/each-e: upstream counts an `{#each}` block's `{:else}` branch as rendered any number of times, so the class selector that selects it once does not report (upstream_issues.md)
consistent-selector-style/valid/keyframe: upstream reads `from` and `50%` inside `@keyframes` as element types (upstream_issues.md)
consistent-selector-style/valid/shorthan: upstream skips a shorthand `{id}`, so the ID selector reports where `id={id}` does not (upstream_issues.md)
no-at-const-tags/valid/rune-in-as-type-i: upstream turns runes mode on for a rune named in `as T`, which names no rune (upstream_issues.md)
no-at-const-tags/valid/rune-in-interface: upstream turns runes mode on for a rune named in an interface, which names no rune (upstream_issues.md)
no-at-const-tags/valid/rune-in-type-alia: upstream turns runes mode on for a rune named in a type alias, which names no rune (upstream_issues.md)
no-dynamic-slot-name/invalid/quote-in-ex: upstream fixes to `name="a"b"`, which ends the value at the inner quote (upstream_issues.md)
no-dynamic-slot-name/invalid/quote-in-qu: upstream fixes to `name="xa"b"`, which ends the value at the inner quote (upstream_issues.md)
no-dynamic-slot-name/invalid/space-in-un: upstream fixes to `name=xa by`, which the space splits into two attributes (upstream_issues.md)
no-not-function-handler/invalid/const-ta: upstream does not follow a `{@const}` declaration, which is as constant as a script's (upstream_issues.md)
no-not-function-handler/valid/destructur: upstream follows `h` to the whole initializer and reports an array, though `h` is 1 (upstream_issues.md)
upstream follows `h` to the whole initializer and reports an object, though `h` is 1 (upstream_issues.md)
no-reactive-literals/invalid/compound-an: upstream suggests `let a += 1` and `let obj.x = 1`, which do not parse (upstream_issues.md)
no-reactive-reassign/invalid/typescript-: upstream stops at a TypeScript cast or `!`, so `(v as any) = 2` and `obj!.a = 3` go unreported (upstream_issues.md)
no-unused-class-name/valid/space-after-e: upstream reports `Unused class ""` for the space after the expression (upstream_issues.md)
no-unused-class-name/valid/space-before-: upstream reports `Unused class ""` for the space before the expression (upstream_issues.md)
no-useless-mustaches/invalid/entity-comp: upstream fixes `&am{'p;'}` to `&`, which the compiler decodes to `&` (upstream_issues.md)
no-useless-mustaches/invalid/entity-in-a: upstream fixes `{'&'}` to `"&"`, which the compiler decodes to `&` (upstream_issues.md)
no-useless-mustaches/invalid/entity-in-q: upstream fixes `{'<'}` to `<`, which the compiler decodes to `<` (upstream_issues.md)
no-useless-mustaches/invalid/entity-in-t: upstream fixes `{'&'}` to `&`, which the compiler decodes to `&` (upstream_issues.md)
no-useless-mustaches/invalid/entity-spli: upstream fixes both halves of `{'&am'}{'p;'}` to `&`, which the compiler decodes to `&`; the first half alone keeps the text (upstream_issues.md)
no-useless-mustaches/invalid/null-escape: upstream fixes `{'\0'}` to `0`, though the string is U+0000 (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-class-directive/invalid/class-wit: upstream writes a second `class:x`, which Svelte rejects as a duplicate attribute (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-const/invalid/script-module-input: upstream treats an `export let` of `<script module>` as a prop and does not report it (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-destructured-store-props/invalid/: upstream takes the property name `a` in `$s.a` for the `{#each}` item `a` (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-destructured-store-props/valid/ea: upstream does not see the `{#each}` item `i` in `$s[i]` (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-style-directive/invalid/condition: upstream drops `!important` from the conditional's value (upstream_issues.md)
upstream moves `color: red` to a directive, which then wins over the later `color: blue` (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-style-directive/invalid/declarati: upstream slices the source by the cleaned value's length and writes `style:color="a /*"` (upstream_issues.md)
prefer-style-directive/invalid/property-: upstream moves `color: red` to a directive, which then wins over the later `Color: blue` (upstream_issues.md)
shorthand-directive/invalid/value-after-: upstream writes `style:color={color}|important`, which the compiler reads as the text `{color}|important` (upstream_issues.md)
